Collect the information about the changes in the lines, which
could be used to minimize the amount of drawing operations.

The user controlled elements, like `Vi` mode cursor and `Selection` are **not** part of the
collected damage state. Those could easily be tracked by comparing their old and new
value between adjacent frames.

After reading damage [`reset_damage`] should be called.

[`reset_damage`]: Self::reset_damage

docstring:
Run LF/NL.

LF/NL mode has some interesting history. According to ECMA-48 4th
edition, in LINE FEED mode,

> The execution of the formatter functions LINE FEED (LF), FORM FEED
> (FF), LINE TABULATION (VT) cause only movement of the active position in
> the direction of the line progression.

In NEW LINE mode,

> The execution of the formatter functions LINE FEED (LF), FORM FEED
> (FF), LINE TABULATION (VT) cause movement to the line home position on
> the following line, the following form, etc. In the case of LF this is
> referred to as the New Line (NL) option.

Additionally, ECMA-48 4th edition says that this option is deprecated.
ECMA-48 5th edition only mentions this option (without explanation)
saying that it's been removed.

As an emulator, we need to support it since applications may still rely
on it.
signature: fn newline(&mut self)

docstring: Build the forward and backward search DFAs.
signature: pub fn new(search: &str) -> Result<RegexSearch, Box<BuildError>>
response:
```rust
pub fn new(search: &str) -> Result<RegexSearch, Box<BuildError>> {
    let syntax = SyntaxConfig::default();
    let thompson = ThompsonConfig::default();
    let config = Config::default();

    let mut regex = RegexSearch {
        left_fdfa: LazyDfa::new(
            search,
            config.clone(),
            syntax,
            thompson.clone(),
            Direction::Left,
            false,
        )?,
        left_rdfa: LazyDfa::new(
            search,
            config.clone(),
            syntax,
            thompson.clone(),
            Direction::Left,
            true,
        )?,
        right_rdfa: LazyDfa::new(
            search,
            config.clone(),
            syntax,
            thompson.clone(),
            Direction::Right,
            true,
        )?,
        right_fdfa: LazyDfa::new(
            search,
            config.clone(),
            syntax,
            thompson.clone(),
            Direction::Right,
            false,
        )?,
    };

    Ok(regex)
}
```
